nodes.description: Two pathogenic XRCC1 alleles. The recurrent c.1293G>C p.(Lys431Asn) sits at the last base of exon 11, in the intron 11 donor splice site, and causes aberrant splicing and reduced XRCC1 mRNA. It was found in trans with the nonsense variant p.(Gln465*) in the first patient, and homozygous in two Pakistani patients from consanguineous families who share a haplotype around the variant. The alleles are hypomorphic: Xrcc1-null mice are embryonic lethal, and the small amount of XRCC1 left in patient cells is thought to allow normal development.

nodes.description: In mice with neural Xrcc1 deletion, cerebellar interneurons (basket, stellate and Golgi cells) are lost through p53-dependent cell-cycle arrest as their progenitors differentiate, granule neurons die by apoptosis, and Purkinje cell spike activity falls. Patients show cerebellar atrophy on MRI, but the cell types lost in human cerebellum have not been examined.

nodes.description: XRCC1 normally limits how long PARP1 stays bound and active at repair intermediates. Without it, PARP1 is trapped on the DNA and overactive, producing excess poly- and mono-ADP-ribosylation. Trapped PARP1 also blocks DNA polymerase beta, which slows repair further. Elevated ADP-ribose is present in patient cells and in the cerebellum of Xrcc1-deficient mice.

evidence.reference_title: XRCC1 mutation is associated with PARP1 hyperactivation and cerebellar ataxia.
